I will do this year much like last year, because on 6 mu I cannot afford to gamble. In Quzhou our wheat-maize rotation is common, and I watch what the better growers around me do. I have well irrigation, so I will push fertilizer a little rather than hold back, because if wheat stools weak or maize ears stay small, that loss is worse than spending a bit more on inputs. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put more fertilizer at the base, then add nitrogen once at greening and once around jointing, with 3 irrigations if the weather is normal. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep the stand even, put part of the fertilizer before or at sowing, then chase nitrogen around the big bell-mouth stage, with 2 irrigations in normal years. I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage because wheat and maize are connected tightly in time, and I need to turn the land fast after harvest. On pesticides, I will not spray too many times, but I will not skip the key timings either: one or two clean sprays for weeds and one or two for disease/insects depending on the field.
